Just randomposting here, but I thought I'd drop this handy fixit I discovered.

In my experience, what breaks on computer chairs most often is the height adjustment valve. I think it's because the seals are cheap, but from what I've seen the standard $100-$120 retail computer chair last about 1-2 years of regular service. I'll buy the Pewdiepie Clutch chair someday, but in the meantime I've been getting by with cheap chairs and this simple hack.

I can't be bothered to post relevant pics because it's a chair, you get the idea. So when the height valve lever thingy fails on your computer chair and the seat slowly sinks to the lowest position each time you sit on it, there is one simple thing you can do to temporarily fix the situation until you can be arsed to buy another computer chair.

What you need is a length of PVC pipe. It's just good stuff to have around if you are at all handy. Measure the length of the chair stem, gauge how far up you want the seat to ride and mark the pipe at that point, then cut it with a saw to length. I use a little mitre block to help keep it in place, but clamps might be better if you have them available, poly-vinyl chloride is a tough and fibrous substance and will readily tug on the blade. Make sure you have ventilation or respiratory filtration, plastic dust is not good medicine.

Once the pipe is cut to length comes the hard part. You have to cut the pipe lengthwise on one side, forming a straight crack you can then pry open and place around the support stem of the chair. This I usually do with a mismatched pair of locking pliers, but if you don't mind a little pain you might be able to accomplish with some oil or grease and your hands.
